name: Zimri and Cozbi
charge: Bringing a Midianite woman into the camp in the sight of the congregation, while the plague ran
summary: While the whole congregation wept at the tabernacle door over the plague, Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites, walked Cozbi the daughter of Zur, a princess of Midian, past them into his tent: a man who did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. Phinehas followed with a javelin and thrust them both through, and the plague was stayed. The charge stands to Simeon to this day.
offenseFull: The people had already joined themselves to Baal-peor, called to the sacrifices of their gods and eating and bowing down, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel (Numbers 25:2-3). Then, while the whole congregation was weeping before the door of the tabernacle and the plague was running, one of the children of Israel came and brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of Moses and of all the congregation of the children of Israel (Numbers 25:6). The Israelites at that door were trying to repent, praying that the judgment would be lifted, and this man came through the middle of it with the woman, hopping and skipping, clueless, without fear. That is what it looks like when a thing has been going on so long that a man no longer cares who sees it; all he cared about was fulfilling his lust, in the middle of a national mourning, while the Most High was passing judgment.

The record names them both deliberately: the Israelite who was slain was Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites, and the Midianitish woman who was slain was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur, who was head over a people and of a chief house in Midian (Numbers 25:14-15). A prince of Israel brought a princess of the other nations into the camp, which is why the two houses are named. It is the mixing the fathers forbade from the beginning: no covenant with those nations and no marriages with them, because they turn a son away from following Him to serve other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4), and a man is to take a wife of the seed of his fathers, because the fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred (Tobit 4:12). The charge stands to Simeon to get it together, and Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes.
judgmentFull: Phinehas rose up from among the congregation with a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel and the woman through her belly; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those who died in the plague were twenty-four thousand (Numbers 25:7-9). The Lord said that Phinehas had turned away His wrath, being zealous for His sake among them, so that He did not consume the children of Israel in His jealousy (Numbers 25:10-11). Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and so the plague was stayed (Psalms 106:30-31).

The judgment then ran outward to the nation that had supplied the women: Israel was to vex the Midianites and smite them, because they vexed Israel with their wiles, wherewith they had beguiled them in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, who was slain in the day of the plague for Peor’s sake (Numbers 25:16-18). Her own people are charged with her, which is how the case is remembered: not one man’s private sin but a stratagem working through a prince and a princess in the sight of the whole congregation.

lawsResolved.text: We are not to intermarry with those who practice idolatry.
Anyone that has served or worshipped false or pagan gods shall be put to death.
It is the will of God that you abstain from fornication and sexual immorality.
It is an abomination for a civil ruler to commit wickedness, for his office is established on righteousness.

text.text: And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.
And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.

And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
Now the name of the Israelite that was slain, even that was slain with the Midianitish woman, was Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites.
And the name of the Midianitish woman that was slain was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur; he was head over a people, and of a chief house in Midian.
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.

Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.
And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand;
And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.
And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy.
Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.
And that was counted unto him for righteousness unto all generations for evermore.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
Vex the Midianites, and smite them:

For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, which was slain in the day of the plague for Peor’s sake.
